title: TWO READERS
rule: one set of facts, two readers: a switch rewrites every line for a hiring manager or for an engineer
description: Seven pieces of work in a log beside one fixed frame, then the own projects. It opens on a shipped product: the Read to Feed store screenshot (logo, My Books, 36% read), with 'Read 36%' ringed for 'It kept each child's place in every book.' Row 02 is the billing report that asked the database 16 times and gave up, and now asks 2 times and finishes. A quiet legend under the identity shows the trick before any click: 'Every line here is written twice. Pick the reader in the bar at the top.', with one real pair ('built once for iPhone and Android' = 'one React Native codebase'). The switch, 'Same facts for: Hiring manager · Engineer', sits in a sticky bar for the whole page and rewrites every line, the own-projects rows included. Own projects: Offday (best-dates suggestions, light), OFFBEAT (the eight-step drum machine) and FORM (the Trefoil with its formula), each a close crop at CSS size from the 2x captures, with GitHub links for the two concepts.
signature: Paper #F3EFE6, ink #1B1A17, muted #5E5A52, one vermilion accent #B8311B (5.2:1 on paper). Newsreader for the plain reader, JetBrains Mono for the engineer: the face change is the signal that the reader changed. The two faces load through the FontFace API; a CSS animation holds the text for at most 250 ms, and a face that comes later is kept for the next visit, so text never rewraps in view (local Georgia and Menlo stand in). Desktop: a 560 px log (identity, sticky switch bar, rows) and a 4:5 frame (573 x 716 at 1440 x 900), sticky, with a count and caption under it. Row 01 plate is the public Read to Feed store screenshot (crop 704 x 880 source px at 0.81, never upscaled); row 02 is a vermilion card ('16' struck, 16 ticks, 'Gave up'; '2', 2 ticks, 'Finished'). Incentiv and Viva Fresh crops end on whole UI parts and stand on a colour sampled from the screen around the crop. Design System v2 shows ready-made buttons and inputs to the hiring manager and the token card to the engineer. Every line is two versions in one grid cell, so a switch never moves the page (CLS 0). Switch: each visible line fades (120 ms, ease-out), then the other reader's words write in with a clip-path wipe (240 ms, ease-out, from 120 ms), top to bottom with a 30 ms stagger; off-screen lines swap at once. The hairline hides at the switch and draws again (180 ms) from the new last word. Rows become current at 42% of the viewport after 160 ms; the plate cross-fades in 200 ms; the line never follows the scroll. Keyboard: arrow keys in the log jump with no travel; the switch is a radio group, and a key switch swaps the words at once. The reader is kept in the URL (?read=engineer). The hook panel and the switch bar are one vermilion block: the top part (the two-reader sample) scrolls away, the bar sticks. The last row keeps the sticky frame whole (column bottom padding). Own projects: percentage crops with a fixed aspect ratio, lazy, CLS 0; Offday 2880 x 1410 source crop, OFFBEAT and FORM 1440 x 836, phone crops from the phone screenshots. Phone: each row carries its own 4:3 plate with the same ring; the bar hides its label below 1280 px so both buttons stay on one row. Reduced motion: words swap at once, the line appears, nothing plays.
holdback: Lowest: harmony and calm, 8/10. The page is still a log beside a sticky frame (a known scrollytelling layout); the switch is the only new idea. Other limits: the Read to Feed store frame is 780 px wide, so the lead crop shows at about 1.76x on a 2x screen (no sharper public capture exists); at 1024 x 768 the row 01 result falls just below the fold (the line and the plate show); on phone the OFFBEAT crop is the 3D speaker from the phone capture, because the drum grid cannot be shown whole at 11 px text in 327 px; Offday has no public link (its repository is private), so its row has none; the engineer h1 keeps the height of the longer plain h1.

chroma.method: scratchpad/chroma6r.mjs logic (review/loop9b/two-readers/chroma-tr.mjs) on review/loop9b/two-readers/final/d-top.png (1440 x 900), captured last. Round 9: 30.4% / 13.0% (the vermilion legend). Engineer view: 15.4% / 0.2%.
